summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for hypoxia and acute respiratory failure due to recurrent tracheal and left mainstem bronchus stenosis from ___ syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. He underwent bronchoscopy with balloon dilation, which improved airway patency and oxygenation. A post-obstructive pneumonia was identified during the procedure, and he was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later discharged on a 7-day course of levaquin. His leukocytosis was consistent with chronic inflammation. A CT scan showed stable airway narrowing, a small post-procedural bleed, and a new area of ground-glass opacity suspicious for early pneumonitis. Fungal cultures grew fusarium and penicillium species, prompting pending serologic testing and an outpatient ID follow-up. He was managed with a steroid taper, pain control, and continuation of home medications. He improved clinically, was weaned to trach mask, and discharged home with follow-up arranged.
